about: Whether this deployment hands construction to a cheaper worker, and which
backend each worker role runs on ([[REQ-295]]).
WHY A FILE OF ITS OWN AND NOT A KEY IN `backends.json`. That file's keys are
the FRAMEWORK'S schema: `configureBackends` validates the whole document at
start-up and rejects a key it does not declare, so an `enabled` flag there
would fail the very validation the file exists to pass. It is not a key in
`instances.json` either — that document says what a ROLE may do, and whether
a deployment composes the delegation surface at all is a fact about the
deployment rather than about any role's authority.
WHAT `enabled: false` MEANS, and it is the whole of the rollback story. The
delegation surface is NEVER COMPOSED — not composed-and-refusing. That is the
shape this repository already gives a missing browser, a missing image
renderer and a missing ticket store: absent rather than present-and-throwing,
so the manual never mentions it, the method prose renders nothing, and the
model cannot propose, apologise for or probe for an operation it has not got.
A deployment with the switch off is indistinguishable from this repository
before delegation existed, which is what makes turning it off a true rollback
rather than a new state to debug.
IT SHIPS ON, and it shipped off first. Two things kept it off. One has been
discharged outright: a worker runs on the smaller context window, and until
REQ-296 landed there was nothing between it and an overflow — now every entry
beside this one resolves a declared window or start-up refuses, so the worker
meets a guard rather than a provider error halfway through a customer's turn.
The other was that REQ-292's meter wanted a period of undelegated records to
measure the saving against, and that one was overruled: the before-figure is
the modelling in the ticket, and waiting a week to be told what construction
costs is itself a week of paying it. The switch remains the rollback.
THIS DOCUMENT IS THE DEPLOYMENT'S POSITION, AND SINCE [[REQ-353]] IT IS WHAT A
BUSINESS INHERITS RATHER THAN THE ONLY VALUE THERE IS. It used to say per-tenant
control was out of scope and that `workers` was a MAP rather than a pair of
scalars so that adding a scope later would be an extension of this document
rather than a rewrite of it. The first half is superseded and the second half is
why the supersession was cheap: a business now says only WHETHER it delegates,
in a table of its own, and that answer is applied to THIS document — so `on`
still means whatever this deployment means by on, and which model a worker runs
on stays a deployment fact with no per-business dimension at all.
STILL READ AT START-UP, AND NOW ALSO PER SCOPE. The bundled import is what a
host with no resolver reads — the `1c` CLI, permanently — and a host that has
one asks it on the path that builds a manager. Both paths go through the same
validation below, so a stored value earns every named refusal this document
already earns.
A worker role bound to a backend `backends.json` does not declare is refused
at start-up naming the role and the backend, rather than at the first
delegation — which is the same rule `configureBackends` applies one file over,
and for the same reason: a configuration failure discovered mid-conversation
is a configuration failure discovered by a customer.
WHAT `primary_writes: false` MEANS ([[REQ-343]]), and it is the second half of
the same question. `enabled` says whether there are workers; this says whether
the consultant still writes now that there are. With it off the consultant
keeps every read, every measurement and every camera and holds none of the
write groups: its route to a change in the site is a brief to a worker and
nothing else. That is DOC-60's end state, and the measured case for it is that
workers did 27% of the element writes for 2.9% of the spend — $0.046 an
element write against $0.54.
IT SHIPS OFF, AND `true` IS THE FLIP-BACK, which is the whole reason it is a
key rather than an edit to `instances.json`. Restoring the consultant's hands
is this one value and a redeploy, not a revert: the grant it goes back to is
the one `instances.json` still states, so nothing has to remember what was
taken away. Absent reads as `false` — the design rather than the state the
design replaced — and the shipped document states it anyway so that an
operator reads the value here rather than deriving it from code.
`enabled: false` DOMINATES IT, and structurally rather than by a check. The
narrowing is applied at exactly the point the delegation surface is composed,
so there is no reachable setting of these two keys where the consultant has
lost its write groups and has no worker to commission — not with the switch
off, and not with the switch on and no worker role bound. The rollback above
stays a true rollback without this document having to say so twice.
WHICH GROUPS GO IS DERIVED AND NOT LISTED HERE. Every group in
`l1-surface.json` declares its `effect`, and the narrowed grant is the
consultant's entry filtered to the ones declared `read`. A write group added
to the surface later is withheld without an edit to this file, and there is no
second list of group names to fall behind the first.
